title: Conjecture 1.1
statement_text: For a $3$-graph $H$, there exists a constant $c$ depending only on $H$ such that $r(H,K_{n}^{(3)})\leq n^{c}$ for all $n$ if and only if $H$ is a subgraph of an iterated blowup of an edge.
context_text: A $k$-graph is a $k$-uniform hypergraph and $K_n^{(k)}$ is the complete $k$-graph on $n$ vertices. The off-diagonal Ramsey number $r(H,K_n^{(k)})$ is the least $N$ such that every red/blue colouring of the edges of $K_N^{(k)}$ contains a red copy of $H$ or a blue $K_n^{(k)}$. A blowup of an edge is a complete tripartite $3$-graph, and an iterated blowup of an edge is either a blowup of an edge or is obtained from one by placing iterated blowups inside one or more of its parts; $H$ is iterated tripartite if it is a subgraph of an iterated blowup. For graphs ($k=2$), $r(H,K_n)$ always grows polynomially, but for $3$-graphs it need not: $r(K_4^{(3)},K_n^{(3)})\ge2^{\Omega(n\log n)}$, and even some linear $3$-graphs have superpolynomial Ramsey numbers. The 'if' direction (polynomial growth for iterated tripartite $H$) follows from work of Erdős and Hajnal; the problem was first raised explicitly by Conlon at an AIM workshop in 2015, and the conjecture proposes a full classification. A $3$-graph is tightly connected if any two edges are joined by a sequence of edges in which consecutive edges share two vertices, and tight components are the maximal tightly connected subgraphs. The authors prove the conjecture for tightly connected $H$ (if $H$ is tightly connected and not tripartite then $r(H,K_n^{(3)})\ge2^{\Omega(n^{2/3})}$) and for $H$ with at most two tight components (if moreover $H$ is not iterated tripartite then $r(H,K_n^{(3)})\ge2^{\Omega(\log^2 n)}$).
notes: First author (Conlon) posed the problem at a 2015 AIM workshop (ref [5]); the formal conjecture as stated here appears to be the paper's own formulation.
paper_title: When are off-diagonal hypergraph Ramsey numbers polynomial?

title: Conjecture 4.2
statement_text: If $k>s$ and $H$ is a $k$-graph which is $s$-tightly connected and not $k$-partite, then there exists a positive constant $c$ such that $r(H,K_{n}^{(k)})\geq t_{s}(n^{c})$, where the tower function $t_{i}(x)$ is defined by $t_{1}(x)=x$ and $t_{i}(x)=2^{t_{i-1}(x)}$ for all $i\geq 2$.
context_text: A $k$-graph is a $k$-uniform hypergraph and $K_n^{(k)}$ is the complete $k$-graph on $n$ vertices. The off-diagonal Ramsey number $r(H,K_n^{(k)})$ is the least $N$ such that every red/blue colouring of the edges of $K_N^{(k)}$ contains a red copy of $H$ or a blue $K_n^{(k)}$. A $k$-graph is $s$-tightly connected if any two edges $e,f$ are joined by a sequence $e=e_0,e_1,\dots,e_t=f$ of edges with $|e_{i-1}\cap e_i|\ge s$ for all $i$, and it is $k$-partite if its vertices can be split into $k$ parts with every edge meeting each part once. The authors prove the case $s=2$: if $k\ge3$ and $H$ is a $2$-tightly connected $k$-graph that is not $k$-partite, then $r(H,K_n^{(k)})\ge2^{\Omega(n^{2/k})}$. They also propose a stronger conjecture: for $k>s$, the Ramsey number of the whole family $\mathcal{H}_s^{(k)}$ of $s$-tightly connected non-$k$-partite $k$-graphs versus $K_n^{(k)}$ is at least $t_s(n^c)$; since $r(K_n^{(s)},K_n^{(s)})\ge r(\mathcal{H}_s^{(k)},K_n^{(k)})$, this would show that the diagonal Ramsey number $r(K_n^{(s)},K_n^{(s)})$ has tower height at least $s-1$, matching the long-standing upper bound and settling perhaps the central open problem of hypergraph Ramsey theory. The authors call this conjecture likely difficult.
paper_title: When are off-diagonal hypergraph Ramsey numbers polynomial?

title: Conjecture 4.3
statement_text: If $k>s$, then there exists a positive constant $c$ such that $r(\mathcal{H}_{s}^{(k)},K_{n}^{(k)})\geq t_{s}(n^{c})$.
context_text: Here $\mathcal{H}_{s}^{(k)}$ is the family of $s$-tightly connected $k$-graphs that are not $k$-partite. This strengthens Conjecture 4.2, since $r(H,K_{n}^{(k)})\geq r(\mathcal{H}_{s}^{(k)},K_{n}^{(k)})$ for any $H\in\mathcal{H}_{s}^{(k)}$. The authors note that if true in general, this conjecture would also determine the tower height of diagonal hypergraph Ramsey numbers, which they describe as perhaps the central open problem in hypergraph Ramsey theory.
notes: The paper proves this conjecture for $s=2$.
paper_title: When are off-diagonal hypergraph Ramsey numbers polynomial?
